key_insight: Sb doping in Cs2BInCl6 double perovskite nanocrystals creates self-trapped excitons whose emission energy and polarization fingerprints can be tuned by Na-to-K alloying.
engineering_relevance: This offers a composition-guided route to engineer lead-free perovskite emitters with controllable color and anisotropic photoluminescence for optoelectronic and photocatalytic devices.
method: Optical spectroscopy on Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with B-site alloying from Na to K
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states and lattice distortions
Time-resolved polarization anisotropy measurements to probe STE wavefunction structure
evidence_signal: PL shifts from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption near 3.8 eV stays nearly unchanged, and measured anisotropy closely matches theory.
watch_item: The strong PL behavior depends on soft-lattice self-trapping, so device stability and reproducibility may be sensitive to composition and structural disorder.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
